sections.label: Set-up

- **What came out.** When the last number is turned, the pod opens: roll a d66 on the drop table (section 11.7). What comes out goes to the fighter who made the last success, and can be taken from them in melee.

scenarios.title: Concord: The Prosecution
scenarios.lore: The doubter said the numbers were wrong. The numbers were wrong. That is not the point.

sections.label: Terrain needed

sections.text: A **doubter** (a bystander) and **two Inspectorate escorts** start at the centre. Roll a d6: on 1-3 they walk toward the edge on the first player's left, on 4-6 toward the edge on their right. **Hazard.** Before deployment, the player who activates first marks one stamp booth as shorted out: the ground within 1 inch of it is **Dangerous** for the whole battle.

sections.label: Battle rules
sections.text:
- **The march.** At the end of each round the escorts walk the doubter 4 inches toward that edge. If an escort reaches the edge with the doubter still in its charge, the prosecution goes ahead: the doubter is gone and nobody wins the winning condition.

If they win they take the doubter and may lead them. With no escort in contact, a Use action is enough.
- **Retaking the doubter.** Escorts who have lost the doubter walk toward them instead of toward the edge. An escort in base contact with the fighter leading the doubter attacks that fighter, then makes an opposed Fight roll against them, as for a capture: if the escort wins, it has the doubter back and the march goes on.
- **The escorts** are attacked like fighters, shot or fought, and cannot be led. If one goes down, the other still walks. If both go down, the doubter is an ordinary bystander.

name: Ballast
alwaysOn: **Always on: Heavy.** Climbing and jumping (up, across or down) are **Tricky (8)**, not Routine, and a fighter who falls on a failed climb or jump takes at least a **glance**, whatever the distance fallen. Hullbacks, and fighters in a frame, climb and jump at Routine as usual.
terrain: **Typical terrain.** Machinery and stacked cargo (heavy cover), steps and loading ramps (raised), bunker hatches (**Powered**), slag (**Difficult**), a weigh-in scale (a marked platform).

events.Event: **A surprise weigh-in.** Weights and Measures stop everyone who is carrying something. Every fighter who carries a scenario item, a drop item or a downed ally is **Flustered**; they stop to argue the weight
**A gravity surge.** The counterweights stutter. Nobody may climb or jump until the end of the round
**A test pulse.** The Control Group tests a pulse from the bunker. Every bot and every fighter in a frame is **Flustered**; the frame locks up

**The counterweights lift.** For a breath, everything weighs nothing. Each fighter may move up to 2 inches in any direction (including straight up onto a piece of terrain within reach), starting with the player who activates first

**A dropped load.** A cargo crane lets go. The player who activates second places a 3-inch piece of heavy cover anywhere on the table that touches no fighter. Fighters within 1 inch of it are moved aside by their owners

**It walks out.** Something the Control Group is not talking about walks out of the hatch nearest the centre, or the centre of the table if there is none: a rogue machine, walking toward a random edge. If a rogue machine is already on the table, nothing happens

scenarios.name: The Weigh-in
scenarios.title: Ballast: The Weigh-in
scenarios.lore: Everything is weighed on Ballast, and everything weighed is taxed. For once, the scale pays you, by the kilo.

sections.label: Terrain needed
sections.text: A **scale** at the centre: a marked platform at least 3 inches across. Any flat piece will do. Four **cargo crates**: any small blocks.

sections.label: Set-up
sections.text: Four crates are scattered within 8 inches of the centre, none touching the scale or each other. **Hazard.** Before deployment, the player who activates first marks one machinery piece as a running press: the ground within 1 inch of it is **Dangerous** for the whole battle.

sections.label: Battle rules
sections.text:
- **Weight.** The first time a crate is lifted, the lifter's player rolls a d6: that is its **weight**. Put the die beside the crate.
- **Hauling.** A crate of weight **1 to 3** is carried like a downed ally (section 5.10): one carrier at half Move, or two at full Move. A crate of weight **4 or more** moves only while two fighters carry it, and then at half Move. Each carrier spends a Pick up action in base contact to take hold. A carrier who goes down drops it.
- **Weighing.** A carrier in base contact with the scale spends a Use action to set the crate on it. A crate on the scale can be lifted off again with a Pick up action.

sections.label: Winning condition

scenarios.title: Plenty: Hijack the Parade
scenarios.lore: The record harvest has been declared again. Everyone has seen the figures. Several crews have been paid by several people to take the float, and not one of them has a plan for what to do with a float.

sections.label: Terrain needed
sections.text: A **float** with a fruit on it: a tray about 4 by 8 inches (a box lid will do).

sections.label: Set-up
sections.text: The float and **two Inspectorate escorts** (the officials) start at the centre. Roll a d6: on 1-3 they head for the edge on the first player's left, on 4-6 for the edge on their right. **Hazard.** Before deployment, the player who activates first marks one irrigation work as burst: a 2-inch-wide strip around it is **Deep water** for the whole battle.

sections.label: Battle rules
sections.text:
- **The parade.** At the end of each round the float moves 3 inches toward the edge it is heading for, pushing aside, prone, anything in its way, and the officials walk with it instead of making their own walk. If it reaches that edge, it stops.
- **Taking the controls.** A fighter in base contact with the float may spend a Use action to prompt the float (section 8.1): a **Tricky (8)** prompt, either mode, or by hand (section 8.1). On a success the float now heads for the nearest point of **their** deployment zone, and keeps going there at the end of each round until someone else takes it. The float cannot be shot or fought.
- **The officials** keep the line: they attack any fighter in base contact with the float. They can be shot and fought like fighters.

sections.label: Winning condition
sections.text: Have the float in your deployment zone when the battle ends. If it is in neither, the side that took the controls last.

sections.label: Prize
sections.text: The prize (10 parts and a finds roll). The counters also pay **5 parts** to the side that took the controls last, win or lose.

sections.label: Deployment
sections.text: Battle lines (section 11.1), whatever the table says. The parade runs along the street between the sides.
